learning: Hypotheses to check in the race: (1) if s-bend and slalom progress rise above about 0.18 with max_error at or below 0.062 m, the look-ahead was limiting turns; (2) if oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.25, the shorter lead needs lower kd or the mass returned to 0.6 kg; (3) if s-bend progress falls below 0.14, the shorter lead is too late for the bends and y should return to 0.05 m.
notes: Complete robot for the sensor-lead test: the Builder's iteration-8 geometry (sensor y 0.03 m, mass 0.5 kg) with the iteration-7 controller unchanged. Per-track progress, max_error and steering_oscillation are requested so the s-bend and slalom can be read apart from the oval.
rationale: The Builder's iteration-8 proposal moves all five sensors from y = 0.05 m to y = 0.03 m and keeps the iteration-7 geometry otherwise: mass 0.5 kg, track 0.10 m, body 0.10 x 0.12 m, x = -0.08 to 0.08 at 0.04 m spacing, and a 0.016 m footprint. I copied that geometry exactly, so any change in the race comes from the sensor lead alone. Sensor lead has not been varied in any earlier iteration, so there is no race evidence for it. The controller stays at the iteration-7 values (kp 6, ki 0.05, kd 0.9, base_speed 1.5, weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2], last_direction). Keeping it fixed isolates the lead change, which the Builder's test plan depends on. The oval steering_oscillation was 0.208 at y = 0.05 and must stay below 0.25. Because the sensors now sit closer to the axle, the controller sees less look-ahead, so the lag may change, and kd is not retuned until the race shows whether that matters. The oval and bend limits are the watch points. I added controller_errors to the Builder's measurement list so that exceptions are visible.
